subject: Discovery readout: benchmark sprint requirements & evaluation logistics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@aiops.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@aiops.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery readout: benchmark sprint requirements & evaluation logistics

Hi Priya / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier — this note captures how we heard your priorities and a pragmatic plan to move to a short benchmark sprint so you can compare options side-by-side. Please read and flag anything we missed.

Key pain points you called out:
- High tail latency on peak inference (p99 spikes above 800ms for 2k-token responses) hitting SLAs for your agent product.
- Cost unpredictability with current TGI-managed endpoints when scaling concurrent agents.
- Need for tenant isolation and auditability for regulated customers (retention controls + access logs).
- Quality gaps vs. your in-house tuned vLLM model on specialized prompt sets (few shot paraphrase/QA).

Current stack we recorded:
- Experimenting with vLLM on self-hosted GPU fleet for low-level tuning and very high throughput tests.
- Using Turf/Hosted TGI endpoints for quick access but seeing cost & latency variability.
- Kubernetes + Redis KV cache for prefix caching; limited prefix reuse today.

Success criteria for the short benchmark sprint (30 days):
1) Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency numbers for the provided prompt set under 1, 4, 8 concurrent workers — target p99 < 350ms for 2k average response size.
2) Throughput: sustained token throughput at target concurrency (we will run 30/60/90 second sustained windows).
3) Cost: estimated token-level cost delta vs your TGI spend (provide per-million-token estimate).
4) Quality parity: match or exceed your vLLM tuned prompts on the internal eval set (we'll run your metric suite; please share).
5) Observability & controls: evidence of per-tenant logs, retention config, and request-level tracing.

What we will deliver from Redwood for the sprint:
- A short evaluation runbook with step-by-step bench commands (attachment: redwood_eval_runbook_v1.pdf).
- A hosted trial environment (Dedicated trial island) with a pinned model variant and telemetry.
- Baseline metric dashboard (latency percentiles, throughput, errors) and raw logs for your team to inspect.
- Cost estimates and a short run-of-cost report at the end of the sprint.

What we need from you to start (ask list):
1) Sample prompt set + holdout eval metrics (JSONL preferred) — you can drop to the Drive link or attach.
2) Target concurrency/traffic profile for the sprint (baseline QPS, concurrency targets).
3) Any redlines for data handling (retention windows, egress limits).
4) Preferred timing for the 2-week benchmark window (we propose starting Mon Jun 1).

Next steps / owners:
- Camila (me): finalize runbook and schedule the Dedicated trial slot once we have prompts and traffic profile.
- Neha (SE): will scope any model-compatibility notes and a quick config checklist.
- Aditya (AE): will follow up on commercial/billing constraints and draft a short MSA addendum for the trial.

If this aligns I'll queue the runbook + a brief technical kickoff for Mon May 25/ Tue May 26 — which time works for your engineers next week?

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_eval_runbook_v1.pdf, sample_prompts_aiops.jsonl
From: Priya Shah <priya@aiops.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@aiops.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery readout: benchmark sprint requirements & evaluation logistics

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. This matches our notes. A few quick clarifications: 

1) For the quality eval we can share a 1k-sample JSONL with labels (we will upload to your Drive link). The metric is exact-match + ROUGE-L for QA prompts.
2) Concurrency targets: steady-state 8 concurrent workers, spike test up to 32 workers for 60s windows.
3) Retention: 30 days for debug logs; 90 days for audit logs (must be exportable to our S3).

We are OK with the proposed sprint timing as long as the environment is isolated and access-controlled. Can you confirm the Dedicated trial will be reachable from our VPC peering (we prefer SNI tunneling)? Also include any procurement steps — we may need an SOW since we're allotted budget for POC work.

Also looping in Samir to get his availability for a short tech kickoff.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering | AIOps Inc.
priya@aiops.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@aiops.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@aiops.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery readout: benchmark sprint requirements & evaluation logistics

Hi Priya / Samir —

Quick technical notes and what we'll attach to the Drive folder today: redwood_eval_runbook_v1.pdf (attached), a sample harness script for your load profile, and a minimal config template to enable per-tenant logging/export. Highlights below: 

- Dedicated trial networking: we support VPC peering and can provide SNI + mTLS endpoints; security team will need a short IP allowlist.
- Model compatibility: we can run your vLLM-ported checkpoints if licensed, but recommended path is Redwood-hosted variant that we can quantize/optimize for latency. If you want to bring your own model, please provide the checkpoint and a small compatibility test (we'll provide the loader).
- Bench specifics: we'll run p50/p95/p99 measurements across these scenarios: cold-start (empty cache), warm-cache (prefix reuse 60%), and spike windows (32 workers).
- Observability: we'll export request traces to your S3 bucket and provide a Grafana view.

Deliverables timeline (tentative):
- Today: upload runbook + harness + sample config to the Drive link.
- Fri May 22: trial environment up and smoke-tested.
- Mon Jun 1: 10-day benchmark sprint (configurable) start.

Attachments included in Drive: redwood_eval_runbook_v1.pdf, sample_prompts_aiops.jsonl, wiring_config_template.yaml

I'll follow up with a short tech kickoff invite once we confirm your team's preferred slot.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
